A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TAH-QUANT. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial additions and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original training-loss curves, throughput measurements, downstream benchmark scores, quantization-error measurements, and component ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and reports additional pretraining, throughput-sensitivity, low-bit quantization, and numerical-stability experiments in the main text and Appendices D–H.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 changes a central component: v1 assigns one precision to every tile belonging to a token, whereas v2 ranks channel-window allocation tiles and permits different precisions within one token. The new allocation size A defaults to the quantization group size G; A=C recovers token-level allocation. This changes the allocation procedure, while retaining group quantization and the pivot-Hadamard transform.

E1.justification: v1's C4 pretraining experiment is replaced by SlimPajama-6B pretraining, and Appendix D adds mathematical-corpus pretraining on Proof-Pile. HellaSwag and MBPP evaluation disappear. MMLU is removed from the main downstream comparison but remains in the group-size ablation, so its coverage is not wholly removed. The four fine-tuning/instruction-tuning datasets and Math-7K verification remain.

E2.justification: The main FP32/FP16, AQ-SGD, and original-Qwen comparators remain. Appendix H newly evaluates NAIVE-4bit against TAH-Quant-4bit for backward gradients. Newly cited methods such as QuaRot and SpinQuant are not evaluated baselines; likewise, Appendix D explicitly says AQ-SGD is only included in the legend, not executed.

E3.justification: The pretraining protocol changes from Qwen2.5-3B/C4 for 6,000 iterations to LLaMA-3.2-1B/SlimPajama training through approximately 6B tokens, with PP=4, sequence length 4096, batch size 256, and held-out perplexity checkpoints. A separate 8B-model protocol and controlled micro-batch/precision sweeps are added. v2 also reports four or eight pipeline stages instead of uniformly eight, changes the downstream average's benchmark composition, and documents an actual backward-precision increase from 8 to 10 bits after instability.

E4.justification: The original group-size, adaptive-allocation, and Hadamard ablations remain. Appendices E–H add throughput sensitivity to micro-batch size and bandwidth, outlier-threshold sensitivity, INT4/INT3 ratio comparisons, an INT2 failure test, and backward-gradient stress tests. The long-horizon NaN investigation adds a concrete failure analysis absent from v1.

E5.justification: v2 adds curves labelled ePDF to the existing quantization-error histograms and specifies a 300-step rolling-mean estimator for pretraining loss in Table 1. These are limited additions to statistical summaries. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or a significance test supporting v2's statistically indistinguishable wording.

E6.justification: New results include 6B-token validation perplexities of 20.64 versus 20.67 for TAH-QUANT and FP16, and step-600 backward-quantization losses of 2.52 versus 6.04 for TAH-Quant-4bit and NAIVE-4bit. C4 and several downstream result entries disappear. Retained downstream scores and GPT-2 throughput values are unchanged; the SFT average changes from 60.9 to 59.32 because benchmark membership changes. The unchanged throughput table gives 4045/751, approximately 5.39× at 100 Mbps, inconsistent with v2's stated maximum of 4.3×.

T1.justification: The convergence assumptions, theorem, corollary, and Appendix C proofs remain substantively unchanged after matching renumbering. v2 adds computational-complexity bounds for pivot selection, entropy ranking, and Hadamard application in Section 3.4, and formalizes allocation tiles and the A=C special case. These are limited mathematical additions, not a new convergence proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statement redefine the allocator as a strict refinement of token-level allocation and newly claim lower quantization error under the same bit budget. They explicitly extend the contribution to from-scratch pretraining. The abstract also recasts 4.3× as throughput speedup over FP32, adds a 1.33× wall-clock claim over AQ-SGD, and narrows the memory claim to avoiding activation-cache overhead. The 3–4-bit and SGD-rate claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations involving within-token heterogeneity, group-size/metadata tradeoffs, and pipeline bubbles. v1's dedicated early-pretraining limitation is removed, while Appendix D qualifies the 8B run through its limited tokens-per-parameter budget. Appendices G–H add low-bit applicability boundaries and attribute the long-horizon NaN event to backward fixed-point precision, reporting recovery at 10 bits.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility information: default allocation/group sizes and the 80/20 precision split, contiguous uint8 packing, approximately 4.41 transmitted bits per element including metadata, profiling settings, and detailed pretraining architecture and optimizer parameters. Appendix H documents gradient scaling and checkpoint recovery. These disclosures go well beyond v1's short training-settings appendix, although no new code-access resource is provided.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds positioning against Subspace Networks, QuaRot, and SpinQuant, distinguishing parameterization constraints and inference rotations from activation communication during training. Additional citations support slow-network settings and the pretraining token-budget discussion. MMLU, HellaSwag, and MBPP references are removed. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much existing prose remain. Targeted rewrites affect the abstract, contributions, allocation explanation, evaluation discussion, and conclusion; computational overhead receives its own subsection. Evaluation instructions move from the table caption into Appendix B, additional appendices are organized by study, and writing/impact disclosures and an additional author are introduced.

P2.justification: v2 consolidates the retained convergence and runtime panels into Figure 2 and merges the two component-ablation figures into Figure 3. It redraws Figure 1 with density overlays and revised axes, narrows the downstream table, and adds a pretraining table, a two-panel pretraining figure, and six supplementary experimental tables. This substantially changes the presentation of the evidence beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's explicitly acknowledged weak pretraining validation through a 6B-token from-scratch experiment with held-out perplexity and an additional 8B-model check. The sensitivity tests, disclosed backward-gradient failure, and implementation details materially improve evidence about applicability and reproducibility. These gains outweigh the narrower downstream comparison, although unsupported statistical-equivalence language and the throughput-speedup inconsistency limit the strength of some claims.
